item.content:encoded:
What hurts this skip the most is the excessive badassery of the virus.

A virus with 100% infection rate and able to survive for years on an object touched by an infected, to spread to others, again, just through contact, and then going undetected for years.

It would simply infect over 98% of human population before the Foundation could as much as detect it, much less put any form of control on it.

By its concept, the Clockwork Virus should have low-infection rates. AIDS, for example, became a huge epidemic with far less resilience, and actually being unable to survive outside the body for more than a second without extremely favorable conditions, and it is an infection that can go undetected for years. The Common Cold is too successful to be easily contained, coming back every year, and it is far behind 100% infection rate.

item.content:encoded:
This just doesn't make any sense to me. It's too hard to suspend disbelief about the machinery actually working. And I don't buy the idea of an outbreak going undetected. There are far too many ways for it to be revealed. This disease would either take over the world or be fought and destroyed - it's too obvious to be missed, and too powerful to be ignored. It may or may not be controllable by humanity, but either way it seems much too big to be hidden by the SCP Foundation. The clumsily contrived secretiveness that it exhibits in mammals doesn't help me enough, in my difficult task of suspending disbelief.

I find this too contrived and implausible to be interesting, and too unbelievable to be scary.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
MIOS, as per the required reading and site rules, no roleplaying is allowed on the site. SCPs are not real. Incident reports like these are unnecessary.

If this is an attempt to ask for edit permission… I really don't think this will help the article at all. If you want to push for it, contact the original author. It's their work; they have the last word on this.

The incident report doesn't really add much to the article except wave around how great your self-insert character is. For example:
- The whole "I have manged to contained all 3 of them with no issues occurring. I did by all myself" bit. You've got a typo, plus no professional reporting an incident would bother mentioning themselves so much. It'd be more like "3 instances were observed; all have currently been contained. Transportation of said instances to a Foundation site is currently pending".
- The [DATA REDACTED] bit just seems like a cop-out of any potentially interesting info. I'd recommend reading over this guide to fix that.
- The line "This would be the first time any natural/man-made disaster actually saved more people than it killed." is completely unnecessary. It's not exactly a straight-up- disaster if it saves people, is it?
- The line "I only study the Earth and other Astronomical Bodies, and I did better than a regular newbie." is again, too self-congratulatory to be taken seriously. Why the random capitalization? Why is a geologist/planetary scientist studying radiation leaks and meltdowns?
- "who want's Saki I'm buying!" should be "Who wants sake, I'm buying!"
- And yet again, "I did get promoted the day before so it's the perfect excuse". We get it. Your character is very successful. That's not really interesting because the reader has no emotional investment whatsoever in them at this point. All we know is that they apparently did everything right and want to throw a party. Why should the reader care?

I wish to make a incident report on SCP-217.

Outbreak Status: Contained

Reported by Researcher M.I.O.S. (Code named):

I have found an outbreak of SCP-217 while I was studying the effects of radiation leaks or meltdowns on or near plate tectonic boundaries, I was surprised at first, but I have manged to contained all 3 of them with no issues occurring. I did by all myself, but there is a problem on where to transport said SCP-217. Which is why they are kept in Air-tight Tungsten creates, and the room was sterilized 100% after incident. I have been through all sterilization requirements, and passed each one after the event. So here is the list of the infected: 1 Praying Mantis, and 2 Spiders as seen below.

There was a search for anymore of "them" (a 100 mile radius) and found 0 traces of any others.
I'm guessing the tsunami brought the virus here, but the radiation from the [Data Redacted] Nuclear Power Plant might have slowed down the rate of infection and possibly killed the virus before it could spread to other species of the population. This would be the first time any natural/man-made disaster actually saved more people than it killed. Either way, the subjects are contained. Hopefully these Tungsten creates will last until we find a place for these Dang things.

I only study the Earth and other Astronomical Bodies, and I did better than a regular newbie. I guess I'll throw a party to celebrate this event*, who want's Saki I'm buying!

*-I'll say it's for a promotion at my Geologic Research Lab, and the funny thing is I did get promoted the day before so it's the perfect excuse!-*

No pictures on the forum, please. - CryogenChaos
